title: Playing tuba in brass bands and parades
summary: Breaux recalls parades with old man Allen, the Joy Williams band and Willie Parker, and playing again after leaving service in 1945.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Parading for Mardi Gras and the clubs

blocks.x: You also mentioned running at tuba, did you ever play tuba much? Oh yeah, I mean that was my first session. I played a lot of orchestra with tuba. You were going to ask about brass bands out on the street, did you ever play any tubas?

Oh yeah, I played with old man Allen across the river before he died, Red Allen's daddy. And I played the street parade with the Joy Williams band. The tuxedos I played a couple times with them. And there was another old man Parker, I played with him a couple times, the old drummer. He's out of the music, he's out of all games now, he's just about too old to get around. The old man Parker lived down on St. Phil Street.

Willie Parker, that's his man. I think the last parade I played was Willie Parker. The last carnival parade I played for the Eleanor Club. I think the last parade they had before the war, after I came out of service, I don't think I fooled with it. Well after I came out of service in 45 I played with Mr. Allen, old man Allen across the river, a couple of fumes, a few parades. And with George Williams I played.
